title: Predicting Risk-adjusted Returns using an Asset Independent Regime-switching Model

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a hidden Markov model (HMM) with Gaussian mixture emissions to predict market regimes (bull, bear, and high volatility) across multiple asset classes. First and second moment features are extracted using exponential weighted moving moments (EWMM) with a span parameter that dictates regime stickiness and turnover. An Expected Sharpe Ratio (ESR) metric is constructed per state, and the predicted ESR (PESR) is generated by combining state probabilities and transition matrices to guide long-only and long/short trading strategies.
extraction.universe: 15 futures contracts spanning commodities, currencies, equities, and fixed income

key_findings: The proposed asset-independent Hidden Markov Model with sticky features accurately detects bull, bear, and high volatility market regimes across multiple asset classes.
The Predicted Expected Sharpe Ratio (PESR) metric successfully improves risk-adjusted returns compared to underlying asset buy-and-hold benchmarks.
Choosing higher spans for the exponential weighted moving moments increases regime stickiness and lowers portfolio turnover.
Long-only strategies consistently improve Sharpe ratios across almost all assets, whereas long/short strategies generate higher absolute returns but with increased volatility.
limitations: The evaluation uses the entire test dataset to predict the hidden state sequence rather than incremental out-of-sample real-time predictions.
Cumulative returns are not always improved even when Sharpe ratios improve, depending on the asset and transaction costs.
